---
title: "Before the course"
aliases:
  - ../eu-frames-three-days/before.html
---

Four things are needed before the course, and each ends in something that you can check: R and the workspaces installed, with their setup checks reporting no failure; the first module on R worked through; the case study read; and the Eurobarometer files of the waves that the paper used downloaded to your machine, for the work on respondents on the third day. The first day teaches the IDE and Quarto live, with the modules on the AR4DS site as its reading, so working through them beforehand gives you a head start but is not needed.

## 1. R and the workspace

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Install R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), download the [workspace of the EU-frames case](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace), and run `R/check_setup.R` until it reports no failure. The first day teaches R, the IDE and Quarto live on the housing-audit file, the running example of the modules on the AR4DS site, so download the [workspace of the housing-audit case](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace) as well and run its setup check too. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met. If the installation will not cooperate, tell the facilitator before the course: the first day leaves time to finish it.

## 2. Getting started with R

[Open Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The module teaches the R that the course asks of you, from a first line of code to a table and a figure. It works on the data of the housing-audit case, a file small enough to look at whole, and its blocks of code run in your browser.

## 3. The case study

[Read the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The case study presents the original study and its data, SCORE and the Multi100 project, the five reanalyses and the replications. Every day of the course works on this case.

## 4. The Eurobarometer files

[Download the Eurobarometer files](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-eurobarometer-files-for-the-individual-level-work){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The work on respondents on the third day needs the Eurobarometer files of the waves that the paper used. They come from the GESIS archive under a free account and on terms that do not allow the files to be passed on, so each participant downloads them to their own machine, and they never leave it. [The GESIS archive](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the module on data sources takes the download screen by screen. The workspace switches the AI features of Positron and VS Code off for its whole folder, for the reason set out in the [section on licensed data](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ai.html#sec-licensed) of the module on AI assistants.

**By the start of the course** you have the setup checks of both workspaces reporting no failure, you have worked through the first module on R, you know what the claim is and how far apart the results of the five analysts are, and the Eurobarometer files are on your machine.
